text:
Luis: hi everyone, excited to join! i'm blocked on Okta SSO. getting an error about conditional access requiring a device certificate. i'm on Windows 11 and connected via my company vpn. also 1Password invite didn't land. who do I bother?

Sam (IT): welcome Luis! :wave: Windows machines should be Intune-enrolled to get the cert. are you on a company-managed laptop or personal? and which VPN client you using?

Luis: personal laptop for now, using the GlobalProtect VPN client. Okta shows: 'Access denied: device must present an Intune certificate for policy "Corporate Devices"'. clicking enroll just returns me to the login screen.

intune-bot: Ticket INTUNE-1187 created for thread 2691000000. Assigned to Sam (IT). Priority: High.

Sam (IT): Quick plan: 1) if you can, disconnect VPN and try enroll over home network (VPN can block MDM enrollment). 2) install Company Portal app and sign in with your redwood account to trigger Intune enrollment. 3) if using a personal device we may need to enable personal-device enrollment in Intune; i will request a temporary exception.

Luis: disconnected VPN and installed Company Portal. When signing into Company Portal it asked for device admin + permissions, i accepted. It then hung at "Applying device configuration" for a few minutes.

Sam (IT): give it a minute. if it stalls, open Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider > Admin and paste any recent errors. I'll raise a temporary policy waiver if enrollment fails.

Luis: pasted the error log snippet here: "Device management enrollment failed: 80180026 (Device not supported by management)"

Sam (IT): that error usually means the account hasn't been allowed for BYOD enrollment. I'm pushing a temporary policy change to allow personal-device enrollment for your account. Hold tight, should be a couple minutes.

Sam (IT): update: policy change applied. Retry Company Portal and reboot if prompted.

Luis: retried, enroll completed successfully. Company Portal shows compliance: Yes.

intune-bot: Intune enrollment complete for user luis@redwood.dev. Issued device certificate for conditional access.

Luis: tried Okta again, now it proceeds further but hits an MFA prompt that loops back to the first screen after i approve via authenticator.

Nate (Security): hi Luis, that MFA loop can happen if the browser blocks third-party cookies or if an extension interferes. Which browser are you using? Also confirm any privacy/tracking blocking settings.

Luis: using Microsoft Edge stable. I have uBlock installed but disabled it for redwood domains. Cookies allowed.

Nate (Security): try an InPrivate window and perform Okta sign-in there; also clear site data for okta.com and redwood.dev. If it still loops, open devtools console to see any JS errors.

Luis: InPrivate worked! Okta accepted device cert and MFA completed. I'm in. Drive shows eng-team folder, but 1Password invite still missing.

1Password-bot: 1Password invite resent to luis@redwood.dev (item: Redwood - New Hire Seat).

Luis: got the invite, accepted and set up account. thanks all.

Maya (People Ops): welcome aboard Luis! i added you to new-hires orientation at 10am and put your laptop reimbursement form in your email. ping me if that wasn't visible.

Sam (IT): closing INTUNE-1187: resolved by enabling personal-device enrollment + Intune cert issuance; note: VPN blocks enrollment flow. Action item: update onboarding KB to mention disconnecting VPN and InPrivate workaround for Edge MFA loop.

Luis: huge thanks everyone, nice first-day rescue team :)
